Synthetic ratings illustrating agreement, offsets and missing scores

Source: R/datasets.R
mfrmr_agreement_data.Rd

Ready-to-load data from the rating-agreement tutorial. Six Persons complete two Tasks, with up to three Raters on each response. Load with data("mfrmr_example_agreement", package = "mfrmr").

Format

A data frame with 35 rows and four columns: Person, Task, Rater, and Score. Each row is one rater's rating of one Person's response to one Task. Scores use the declared categories 0–3.

Source

Existing data from the rating-agreement tutorial. The deterministic construction is retained in data-raw/make-teaching-data.R in the source repository.

Details

Rater R2 always scores one category above R1, so their rankings agree but their scores differ. R3 has two deliberately different scores, one missing score (P06/T2) and one absent row (P02/T2). There are 34 observed scores. Missing ratings are not zero scores; an absent row alone does not identify whether a rating was planned. Use unit = c("Person", "Task") to match responses. unit = "Person" would mix two different responses.

These are constructed teaching data, not empirical records, expert standards or evidence of a method's performance in a population.

See also

pairwise_kappa_table(), krippendorff_alpha_table(), gwet_ac2_table(), pairwise_icc_table(), load_mfrmr_data()

Examples

data("mfrmr_example_agreement", package = "mfrmr")
ratings <- mfrmr_example_agreement
head(ratings)
#>   Person Task Rater Score
#> 1    P01   T1    R1     0
#> 2    P01   T2    R1     1
#> 3    P02   T1    R1     2
#> 4    P02   T2    R1     0
#> 5    P03   T1    R1     1
#> 6    P03   T2    R1     2
with(ratings, table(Rater, Score, useNA = "ifany"))
#>      Score
#> Rater 0 1 2 3 <NA>
#>    R1 4 4 4 0    0
#>    R2 0 4 4 4    0
#>    R3 3 4 3 0    1
agreement <- pairwise_kappa_table(ratings, rater = "Rater",
  unit = c("Person", "Task"), score = "Score", categories = 0:3)
agreement$table
#>   Pair Rater1 Rater2  N CandidateUnits ExcludedUnits     Kappa    Status
#> 1    1     R1     R2 12             12             0 0.5714286 available
#> 2    2     R1     R3 10             12             2 0.8333333 available
#> 3    3     R2     R3 10             12             2 0.4545455 available
#>   Weighting ObservedAgreement ExpectedAgreement ScaledObservedDisagreement
#> 1 quadratic         0.8888889         0.7407407                  0.1111111
#> 2 quadratic         0.9777778         0.8666667                  0.0500000
#> 3 quadratic         0.8666667         0.7555556                  0.1333333
#>   ScaledExpectedDisagreement
#> 1                  0.2592593
#> 2                  0.3000000
#> 3                  0.2444444
# Each pair uses its own shared responses; inspect its denominator as well.
